question: which ring in the radial intensity profile is the lens edge, and what is the lens diameter in pixels
micron_free: no micron figure appears anywhere in this file or its siblings. Turning pixels into microns needs the client nominal and is Phase 2 and 3 work.

discriminator_1_missing_lens.label: P1_NL = missing_lens, 53 sampled pictures with a measured cavity

discriminator_2_lens_off_center.label: P2_LOC = lens_off_center, 199 sampled pictures with a measured cavity
discriminator_2_lens_off_center.note: the offset is the ring centre less the cavity centre, measured from the 360 ray dips; the cavity centre is the shipped bright-blob centroid, the same origin the radial profile uses

lens_diameter_px.headline_method: least-squares circle fit to 360 radial edge points restricted to 0.80-0.96 of the cavity radius, outlier-rejected

verdict.structural_argument: the cavity wall is where the bright disc ends, and the shipped mask already puts that boundary at R_cav (median 438.5 px radius, 877.0 px diameter). A dark feature at 1.01 R_cav is therefore at the wall, not inside the cavity, and cannot be a free-floating lens rim; a lens whose rim sat on the wall would fill the cavity exactly, which the existence of a Lens Off Center class contradicts. The only ring clear of the wall is the one at 0.89 R_cav, and that is the lens edge.
verdict.discriminator_1_outcome: DECISIVE for the ring family, not for a single ring. Every outer dark ring, both candidates, is present only when a lens is present.
verdict.discriminator_2_outcome: INCONCLUSIVE. The P2_LOC tag does not move either ring's centre relative to the cavity centre, so no ring can be assigned by motion.
verdict.the_848_px_figure: REPRODUCED. The wide-band least-squares circle fit, 0.50 to 1.06 of R_cav, gives a median 841.4 px over the same library population (the earlier figure was 848). It is a blend of the two modes, not a single physical ring: restricted to the rim band the same fit gives 789.0 px.
